rv.q: This odd little show has charm aplenty, though for some it may also prove something of a well-intentioned dog’s dinner.
Giving human voices to pets was something of a double-edged sword in this case.
Even his skills can’t salvage this show.
Every dog has its day and, if the audience’s warm, laughter-filled reaction is anything to go by, this play will certainly have many more bright days in its future.
Dog Mom is a charming, if somewhat uneven, production... the production never quite turns its charming premise into something theatrically distinctive.
Dog Mom has bags of heart, but it could dig deeper.
By taking itself a touch too seriously, “Dog Mom” weakens the messages that are better served with humour.
Well meaning canine comedy goes astray.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this canine comedy, with praise for the charming dog characters but criticism for underdeveloped humans and an uneven tone that struggles to balance whimsy with its heartfelt themes about motherhood and companionship.
